title: How to Use Autodesk Assistant in Revit 2025: Alternatives
summary: Revit 2025 lacks the built-in Autodesk Assistant. Explore ArchiLabs for native model editing and an equipment-register update in your existing release.
body_markdown:
You've seen a video of someone asking Revit to create a schedule or find elements in a model. You open your own project, look for the same Assistant panel, and can't find it. If you're using Revit 2025, the missing button has a straightforward explanation: the video is showing a newer version.


## How to use Autodesk Assistant in Revit 2025


Autodesk's built-in Revit Assistant is available in **Revit 2027 and later** . It isn't part of Revit 2025, and there isn't a setting that turns it on in that release. Autodesk confirms the version restriction in its[support guidance for earlier Revit versions](https://help.autodesk.com/view/RVT/2026/ENU/?caas=caas%2Fsfdcarticles%2Fsfdcarticles%2FHow-to-enable-Autodesk-Assistant-feature-available-in-Revit-2025.html) .


So a Revit 2027 tutorial can't be followed in 2025, and reinstalling or repairing 2025 won't make the panel appear.


In Revit 2027, Assistant can answer product questions, query model information, and make supported changes. Autodesk's[November update](https://www.autodesk.com/blogs/aec/2026/11/10/whats-new-in-revit-2027-3-and-2027-4/) describes schedule editing, graphics changes, and help building and running Dynamo graphs. Some Assistant improvements arrive through service updates, while the newer Dynamo tools depend on your installed release.


## Why upgrading isn't always the answer


For a new project, moving to a newer Revit release may be an option. An active project is a different situation. A model saved in a newer Revit release[cannot be opened in an older one](https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/Backwards-compatibility-of-Revit-with-earlier-releases-of-the-software.html) . Your consultants may still be working in 2025, your office may have standardized its add-ins around that release, and the project team may have agreed to keep the model there until the next milestone.


Getting access to one AI feature doesn't automatically make that coordination work worthwhile. The more useful question becomes: can you get AI assistance while continuing to work in Revit 2025?

## What that looks like in everyday Revit work


Consider a manufacturer specification that needs to become a Revit family. Normally, someone reads the PDF, finds the dimensions, builds the object, adds the required information, and places it in the project. Even a fairly simple piece of equipment can take time because the information has to move from the document into the model.


ArchiLabs Desktop brings those steps into the same conversation. You provide the source document and describe what you need. Our[equipment-modeling recording](https://archilabs.ai/desktop) shows a manufacturer PDF becoming a native Revit family and then being placed in a project. Where the PDF left a dimension out, it was approximated, and the video has been edited to cut out waiting time.


Because the result is a native Revit family, it behaves like any other family in the project. When the specification changes again, you can open it, adjust it, and keep tagging and scheduling it as usual.


The same idea applies to existing model data. If an approved spreadsheet changes equipment descriptions, the job is to match those rows to the right model elements and update the relevant fields. You can read more about that task in our[Excel-to-Revit parameter guide](https://archilabs.ai/posts/excel-equipment-register-revit-reconciliation) .
